choices.text: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem
Energy flows one way and leaves as heat
Energy cycles between air and plants like carbon

questions.feedback: That trap reading is the one to unlearn: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem. Reteach point: Energy flows one way - sunlight in, heat out: what is recycled is matter - carbon, nitrogen and water.
questions.misconception: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem.
questions.prompt: Which statement about energy in an ecosystem is true?

questions.answer: About 2 000 kJ reaches primary consumers and about 200 kJ reaches secondary consumers: about 10% moves up each level.
questions.feedback: Scene s3 locks the rule: only about 10% moves up each trophic level, so multiply by a tenth at each step and the dot shrinks as it climbs.
questions.prompt: Producers hold 20 000 kJ. Estimate the energy reaching primary consumers and secondary consumers, showing the rule you used.

questions.feedback: Scene s4 shows the blue dot dropping into plants with photosynthesis, then rising back with respiration and combustion.
questions.prompt: In the carbon cycle, which process draws carbon dioxide out of the air and into living tissue?

questions.answer: Corridors reconnect isolated fragments, so individuals and genes can move between populations again.
questions.feedback: Scene s5 ends with the protected corridor linking all three fragments: reconnecting habitat lets species move and interbreed again.
questions.prompt: State how protected corridors help conserve species in fragmented habitats.
